scope.scopeNotesMd: This report compares the R4 and R6 core `StructureDefinition/ContactDetail` artifacts and their local elements: `ContactDetail`, `ContactDetail.name`, and `ContactDetail.telecom`. The R6 artifact is present at the expected canonical URL and file path, so no rename, split, merge, or removal was needed to establish identity. Snapshot differences for inherited `id` and `extension`, and the R6 shift from direct `Element` derivation to derivation through `DataType`, are treated as base/infrastructure changes under the assignment's inherited/base-artifact scope rule.

narrativeReportMd:
# ContactDetail R4→R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
No local material breaking changes were found for `ContactDetail`. The local content model remains `name` (`0..1` `string`) and `telecom` (`0..*` `ContactPoint`) with the same local definitions, cardinalities, types, and summary/modifier flags.

## Scope
The analysis covered the R4 and R6 core `StructureDefinition/ContactDetail` artifacts and compared the local differential and snapshot elements owned by ContactDetail. Inherited `id`/`extension` behavior and the R6 insertion of `DataType` between ContactDetail and `Element` are intentionally excluded from `findings[]` because those are base-artifact changes.

## Main migration themes
R4 instances that use only the ContactDetail local payload can be represented in R6 without a ContactDetail-specific transform, and R6 ContactDetail local payload can be represented back in R4. Implementers should still review generated datatype inheritance if their code generator models R6 `DataType` as a distinct superclass.

## Highest-impact findings
There are no local Critical, High, Medium, or Low findings for ContactDetail.

## Findings requiring human review
No ContactDetail-local finding requires human review. The main caveat is that official narrative diffs were not available, and the R6 package is a ballot build.

## Backward-compatible design observations
The ContactDetail local element model appears intentionally preserved. Metadata and packaging details were refreshed, but the backward-compatible payload shape was retained.

## Follow-up analysis
Datatype hierarchy and inherited Element/Extension validation changes should be handled by the `DataType`, `Element`, and `Extension` reports rather than duplicated here.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: No ContactDetail-local breaking changes were found. The canonical artifact remains present in R6, and the local `name` and `telecom` elements retain the same cardinalities, types, and semantics. The main uncertainty is outside this artifact: generated-code effects from the R6 `DataType` superclass should be assessed in the base datatype reports.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration of ContactDetail payloads should be straightforward: preserve `name` as `string` and each `telecom` entry as `ContactPoint`. No local element rename, removal, new mandatory element, binding change, or choice-type change was identified. Systems with strict model inheritance or validators that depend on snapshot-inherited base constraints should consume the separate base-artifact assessments.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for the local ContactDetail conclusion because both primary StructureDefinitions are present and the local differential elements are unchanged except for non-payload metadata on the root differential element. Confidence is not absolute because no official change log or rendered R4/R6 narrative diff was supplied, and the R6 input is a ballot build.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: The canonical URL, id, name, kind, type, derivation, status, and abstract flag are preserved. The `baseDefinition` changed from `Element` to `DataType`, but that is treated as a base datatype hierarchy change rather than a local ContactDetail identity break.
The local ContactDetail-owned elements remain `ContactDetail`, `ContactDetail.name`, and `ContactDetail.telecom`; no local element was added, removed, renamed, moved, split, or merged.
`name` remains `string`; `telecom` remains `ContactPoint`. There are no choice types on ContactDetail.
ContactDetail has no local `Reference`-typed elements, so no reference target comparison applies.
ContactDetail has no local terminology bindings in either R4 or R6.

No ContactDetail-local differential constraint was added, removed, or changed. Snapshot differences involving `ele-1`, inherited `extension`, `ext-1`, and xpath metadata are inherited/base-artifact concerns and are excluded from local findings.
No fixed value, pattern, or default value appears on the local ContactDetail elements in either version.
No local minValue, maxValue, maxLength, or regex limit was identified for ContactDetail.
The root and local child elements are not modifiers in either version.
`name` and `telecom` remain summary elements; inherited `id` and `extension` remain non-summary.
No ContactDetail-local slicing is present. The inherited slicing on `extension` is out of scope.

The local element `short`, `definition`, and `comment` text for `name` and `telecom` is unchanged. The StructureDefinition-level description was cosmetically shortened, which is recorded as a non-breaking notable metadata change.

No local JSON/XML element names, primitive/datatype choices, multiplicities, or summary/modifier flags changed. Code generators that expose R6's `DataType` superclass may see inherited class hierarchy differences, but that is a base-artifact issue.

Every R6 ContactDetail local payload shape using `name` and `telecom` is representable in R4 at the ContactDetail level. R6-only behavior inherited through base datatypes or through contained `ContactPoint` changes is delegated to those artifacts.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: StructureDefinition metadata was refreshed without changing the local payload model
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R6 changes metadata such as package version, publisher, workgroup extension, jurisdiction, generated narrative, explicit `experimental: false`, and the top-level description prefix from `Base StructureDefinition for ContactDetail Type` to `ContactDetail Type`. These fields affect conformance-resource metadata rather than the JSON/XML shape or validation of ContactDetail instances.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Tools that compare or display StructureDefinition metadata may see differences, especially around publisher and extensions. Payload mappers and validators should not require a ContactDetail-specific data transform for these metadata changes.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 ContactDetail no longer repeats the R4 normative-version extension on the ContactDetail StructureDefinition
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R4 includes `structuredefinition-normative-version` with value `4.0.0` on the ContactDetail StructureDefinition/root differential metadata, while the R6 ContactDetail artifact retains standards-status `normative` but does not repeat that extension at the ContactDetail artifact level. This is metadata about the definition, not an instance element or validation rule for ContactDetail payloads.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Conformance tooling that keys maturity or normative history from this extension should consult the R6 specification's normative metadata conventions rather than interpreting the absence of the extension as a ContactDetail instance-model change.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: R6 ContactDetail derives from `DataType` instead of directly from `Element`. Any breaking impact on generated superclass hierarchies, validators, or inherited constraints belongs to the DataType assessment.

Snapshot differences for inherited `id`, `extension`, `ele-1`, and xpath/condition metadata are inherited from base Element infrastructure and should not be duplicated as ContactDetail-local findings.

The R4 ContactDetail snapshot includes inherited extension-related constraint metadata that is not present in the same way in the R6 ContactDetail snapshot. Any material impact should be assessed in the Extension/base Element reports.
`ContactDetail.telecom` continues to use `ContactPoint`. Any breaking changes inside ContactPoint would affect ContactDetail users indirectly but are owned by the ContactPoint report.
